title: Hypergraph Regularity Core Definitions
description: Core definitions for hypergraph regularity: k-uniform hypergraphs, k-partite density, and epsilon-regularity. Generalizes graph regularity (SzemerediCore) to the hypergraph setting of Gowers (2007).

overview.historicalContext:
Szemerédi's regularity lemma (1975) for graphs is one of the most powerful tools in combinatorics, but many applications require a hypergraph version. The challenge is that naive generalizations of graph regularity to hypergraphs fail: knowing that pairs of vertex sets have uniform density does not suffice to count k-uniform structures.

Gowers (2007) and independently Rödl–Skokan (2004) and Nagle–Rödl–Schacht (2006) solved this by introducing regularity relative to an underlying simplicial complex. In their framework, a k-uniform hypergraph is regular not when large vertex subsets preserve density, but when restricting to dense sub-complexes of the (k-1)-skeleton preserves density. This relative regularity is what makes the hypergraph counting lemma work.

This module formalizes the foundational definitions: k-uniform hypergraphs, k-partite density via transversals, and the naive epsilon-regularity condition. The naive version captures the density-deviation idea and specializes to the graph case (k=2), serving as a stepping stone to the full Gowers regularity.
overview.problemStatement:
Define the core concepts for hypergraph regularity:

- **k-uniform hypergraph**: edges are k-element subsets of V
- **k-partite density**: $d_k(H; V_1,\ldots,V_k)$ = fraction of transversals that are edges
- **Epsilon-regularity**: density is stable under restriction to large subsets

Prove that k-partite density lies in $[0,1]$ and equals 0 for the empty hypergraph.
overview.text: Core definitions for hypergraph regularity: k-uniform hypergraphs, k-partite density, and epsilon-regularity. Generalizes graph regularity to the hypergraph setting.
overview.proofStrategy:
The module provides definitions and four proved lemmas:

1. **edgeCount_empty**: The empty hypergraph has 0 edges (by simp).
2. **kPartiteDensity_nonneg**: By positivity of both numerator and denominator.
3. **kPartiteDensity_le_one**: The filtered set (edges that are transversals) is a subset of all transversals, so its cardinality is bounded.
4. **kPartiteDensity_empty**: The empty hypergraph has no edges, so the filter is empty.

The fromSimpleGraph bridge uses Finset.card_pair with the irreflexivity of adjacency.
keyInsights: k-partite density via transversals naturally generalizes bipartite edge density: for k=2, a transversal of [A, B] is a pair {a, b} with a ∈ A, b ∈ B

The naive regularity condition (density stable under large subset restriction) is correct for graphs but insufficient for hypergraphs — the full Gowers version requires relativization to (k-1)-complexes
Centralizing UHypergraph prevents the 27+ per-problem definitions scattered across Erdős problem files from diverging
The density bounds [0,1] are the hypergraph analogues of edgeDensity_nonneg and edgeDensity_le_one from SzemerediCore

sections.title: k-Uniform Hypergraph
sections.summary: Defines UHypergraph V k: a k-uniform hypergraph with edges as k-element Finsets. Includes edgeCount, the empty hypergraph, and edgeCount_empty.

sections.title: k-Partite Density
sections.summary: Defines transversals (k-sets picking one element from each part) and kPartiteDensity (fraction of transversals that are edges). Proves density is in [0,1].

sections.title: Hypergraph Epsilon-Regularity
sections.summary: Defines IsHypergraphRegular: a k-tuple is ε-regular if restricting each part to a subset of size ≥ ε|Vᵢ| changes density by at most ε. This is the naive generalization of graph regularity.
sections.mathContext: $(V_1,\ldots,V_k)$ is $\varepsilon$-regular for $H$ if for all $V'_i \subseteq V_i$ with $|V'_i| \geq \varepsilon|V_i|$: $|d_k(H; V'_1,\ldots,V'_k) - d_k(H; V_1,\ldots,V_k)| \leq \varepsilon$.

sections.title: Empty Hypergraph Density
sections.summary: Proves that the k-partite density of the empty hypergraph is 0.

sections.title: Bridge to Graph Case
sections.summary: Constructs a 2-uniform hypergraph from a SimpleGraph, connecting the hypergraph framework back to the graph regularity pipeline.
sections.mathContext: For a simple graph $G$, the 2-uniform hypergraph has edges $\{\{u,v\} : uv \in E(G)\}$.

crossReferences.description: Generalizes graph regularity definitions (edgeDensity, IsEpsilonRegular) to k-uniform hypergraphs (kPartiteDensity, IsHypergraphRegular)
The graph regularity lemma uses SzemerediCore definitions; a future hypergraph regularity lemma would use these definitions
The graph counting lemma exploits graph regularity; the hypergraph counting lemma (Nagle-Rödl-Schacht 2006) would need the full Gowers regularity built on these foundations

conclusion.summary: This module provides core definitions for hypergraph regularity in 175 lines with 3 definitions (UHypergraph, kPartiteDensity, IsHypergraphRegular) and 4 proved lemmas (0 sorries, 0 axioms). It generalizes the graph regularity framework of SzemerediCore.lean to k-uniform hypergraphs.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: Hypergraph regularity is the foundation for the multidimensional Szemerédi theorem (Gowers 2007), the hypergraph removal lemma, and many results in additive combinatorics. The naive regularity defined here captures the density-deviation idea and specializes correctly to the graph case.

The centralized UHypergraph structure can replace the 27+ per-problem hypergraph definitions scattered across Erdős problem files, preventing definition drift.

**Limitations**: The naive regularity is insufficient for most applications — the full Gowers regularity (relative to simplicial complexes) is needed for the hypergraph counting lemma and removal lemma.
